Regular tilings and honeycombs from Coxeter reflections

Source: R/layers-coxeter.R
stat_tiling_3d.Rd

Factors the simplex Gram matrix with off-diagonal entries -cos(pi/m). Mirror reflections generate a seed cell and its orbit. Cell centres are deduplicated and retained within radius of the seed centre. Reports the number of cells before emission. Spherical, Euclidean and compact hyperbolic symbols are supported. Ideal or hyperideal vertices and cells require homogeneous clipping or an explicit truncation and raise an error.

Usage

stat_tiling_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  schlafli = c(7, 3),
  radius = 2,
  what = c("edges", "faces", "cells"),
  max_cells = 10000L,
  model = NULL,
  munch_tolerance = 0.001,
  munch_max_depth = 9L,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

stat_honeycomb_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  schlafli = c(5, 3, 4),
  radius = 2,
  what = c("edges", "faces", "cells"),
  max_cells = 10000L,
  model = NULL,
  munch_tolerance = 0.001,
  munch_max_depth = 9L,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

schlafli

Two entries {p,q} for tilings, three {p,q,r} for honeycombs.

radius

Centre distance cutoff in intrinsic units (radians on spheres).

what

Geometry to emit: edges, faces or cells.

max_cells

Explicit orbit resource limit; exceeding it raises an error.

model

NULL chooses Klein, embedded spherical or Cartesian output. Other choices are Poincare for hyperbolic geometry and stereographic for S^3.

munch_tolerance, munch_max_depth

Shared geodesic sampling controls.

Value

A ggplot2 layer with cell and depth computed variables; depth counts simplex reflections.

Details

Hyperbolic output uses the Klein model by default; Poincare output is adaptively tessellated. Spherical tiles lie on S^2. Spherical honeycombs are projected from S^3 into R^3 by their first three coordinates or by stereographic projection. Their curved edges and faces use the shared space sampler. what="faces" deduplicates shared faces, what="cells" retains each cell's boundary, and what="edges" deduplicates shared edges.

References

Nelson and Segerman (2016). Visualizing hyperbolic honeycombs. https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.02851. Kopczynski and Celinska-Kopczynska (2020). https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.09533.

Examples

ggplot2::ggplot()+stat_tiling_3d(schlafli=c(7,3),radius=2)+
  coord_3d(axes=character(),panes=character(),box="none")
ggplot2::ggplot()+stat_honeycomb_3d(schlafli=c(5,3,4),radius=1,what="faces")+
  coord_3d(axes=character(),panes=character(),box="none")
